note: Upstream README benchmark/resource values are reported by upstream; this manifest pins source bytes but does not benchmark GT-1/ESC2.

a2lite_instruction_set_evidence.classification: upstream source inspection; describes available implementations, not ESC2 compatibility or timing

optimized_path.assembly_macro_default: NAM_M7_ASM=1 when the above condition holds; otherwise 0
instruction_set_notes: uses VMAXNM, which README says Cortex-M4F FPv4 lacks

fallback_path.selection: C tiles are compiled when NAM_M7_ASM=0; README explicitly says use this for M4F or any target without FPv5
fallback_path.same_output_claim: README says the C tiles give the same output but run slower
fallback_path.fused_multiply_add: NAM_FMA uses __builtin_fmaf only when compiler macros indicate FMA; otherwise it expands to multiply plus add
fallback_path.architecture_implication: The source is not inherently limited to Thumb-2 if an appropriate C compiler/runtime and scalar floating-point implementation exist; target performance and numeric behavior require measurement/validation.

limitations: A C fallback does not establish that a vendor ESC2 compiler can build the code.
A fallback compile would not establish real-time feasibility, memory placement, or equivalence under the GT-1 pipeline.
The C-versus-assembly performance difference is not quantified for ESC2.

cortex_m7_benchmark_path.classification: upstream source and documentation inspection; benchmark-path attribution is an inference because no board build log or compiled object is retained

documented_measurement.board: Electrosmith Daisy Seed / STM32H750 Cortex-M7 at 480 MHz

default_board_build.tuning_suffix: empty; selects engines/cortex-m7/a2lite rather than a2lite-b16
default_board_build.memory_placement: engine code in ITCM; capture and instance in DTCM; state in AXI SRAM (per upstream README and Daisy benchmark source)

assembly_path_attribution.interpretation: Given the documented Cortex-M7 board and recommended ARMv7E-M/FMA/Thumb-2 flags, the 4059 cycles/sample result is strongly indicated to use the optimized Thumb-2/FPv5 assembly path. The exact preprocessor result is not independently confirmed without the original compile command, log, or object file.
assembly_path_attribution.fallback_cycle_measurement_note: README says the C tiles produce the same output but run slower; it publishes no C-fallback cycle count.

host_benchmark_scope.interpretation: The host build is for correctness/output checking, not the published M7 cycle figure; absent ARM target macros, its source defaults to C tiles.
